Task: T1-10 + T1-12 (emergency beat) + tap-the-dog reactions. Branch cb/emergency-beat.

SETUP
- Work in a separate worktree so other tools keep their checkout:
  git fetch && git worktree add ../pawtner-emergency -b cb/emergency-beat origin/main
  then run npm install in the worktree root and in mobile/.
- Read CLAUDE.md, PRD.md §7.3–7.6 and §13 beat 2, docs/HANDOFF.md first.
- Do NOT modify anything in shared/. Import from it.

PART A — T1-10 blood-pressure log (mobile/src/screens/HealthScreen.tsx)
1. Replace the one-tap "Log" with a small form: systolic, diastolic (inputMode="numeric"), optional note (text). Visible <label>s, touch targets ≥ 48px, all text from en.json.
2. On submit, build a HealthMetric (shared/contract.ts) with recordedAt = now, then ask for a decision (Part B). Keep setting bpLogged so the heart bonus still works.
3. Show the result under the form: the decision's `wording` (it comes from shared/templates.ts; never write the 995 text in a component or in en.json). For emergency_995 and see_gp_soon: calm, plain card, no animation, no emoji, large readable text. For emergency_995 show "995" large, but do NOT make it a tel: link (demo safety: no accidental real calls).
4. Validation: both numbers required, whole numbers in a plausible range (put the range in mobile/src/config/, not inline). Show an inline error, never crash.

PART B — Agent decision, mock for now (one place to swap for the API later)
1. New mobile/src/lib/agent.ts exporting `async function requestDecision(input: AgentInput): Promise<AgentDecision>`. Today it returns decide(buildAgentInput(input)) from shared/rules + shared/selectors. Add a `TODO(T1-07): POST /agent/decide` comment. No component calls decide() directly.
2. A small helper in the same file builds the AgentInput from App state (doses, health metrics, heart, dog name/id from mock data). No names hardcoded.
3. App.tsx keeps `latestDecision: AgentDecision | null` and replaces `selectDogMood(heartCount, null)` with `selectDogMood(heartCount, latestDecision)`, so 185/120 + "bad headache" turns the dog attentive on every screen. A page reload resets it (mock state); say so in the report.

PART C — T1-12 decision log card
1. New presentational component mobile/src/components/DecisionLogCard.tsx (+ .css), props: { decision: AgentDecision }. Shows: rule (ruleId), what it noticed (observations as label/value rows), reasoning, and wording source ("Fixed template, no AI" vs "AI-worded", labels in en.json).
2. Observation labels come from en.json keys (decisionLog.observation.<key>), falling back to the raw key if missing.
3. Render it on Health under the result, collapsed behind a "Why?" button (keyboard-accessible, aria-expanded).

PART D — Tap the dog: rotating reactions
1. New mobile/src/config/pet.ts: the order ["hop", "hearts", "bubble", "bark"], each reaction's duration, the bark sound path ("/assets/bark.mp3"), and a sound on/off flag. No timings or paths inside components.
2. New hook mobile/src/lib/usePetReaction.ts that owns the rotation index, the cooldown (ignore taps while a reaction is playing) and the audio side effect. Rules:
   - mood "attentive" → tapping does nothing playful (no reaction at all).
   - prefers-reduced-motion → rotate only through bubble and bark.
   - bark → skipped if the audio file fails to load or sound is off; never throw. Do not add or download any audio file yourself.
3. DogStage stays presentational: it receives the current reaction as a prop and renders it. Replace the faint wiggle with:
   - hop: a short jump with squash (transform only).
   - hearts: 2–3 small hearts (existing Icon) rise and fade (transform + opacity). Decoration only; they never change the heart score.
   - bubble: a speech bubble above the dog with one of 3–4 lines from en.json (pet.lines.*), rotating, using {{name}} interpolation from data where a name is used. Announce it with aria-live="polite". The bubble must not cover the top bar buttons.
4. Animate only transform and opacity; still fallback under prefers-reduced-motion.

CHECKS AND PROOF
- Root: npm run typecheck, npm run test:unit. mobile/: npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build. All must pass.
- Screenshots at 360x740, 390x844, 430x932, 1280x800 of: Health form; the 185/120 + "bad headache" result with the attentive dog; the decision log open; each pet reaction (hop mid-jump, hearts, bubble). Also one at 360x640 to check the bubble against the top bar.
- Save screenshots of this CodeBuddy chat to proof/.
- Commit in logical steps (BP form + agent; decision log; pet reactions). Do not push or open a PR. Stop and report: files changed, check results, screenshots, anything you couldn't do, and open questions.
</user_query>"}]}

{"requestId":"07d8f69feead4f77999e4c7d90e2ac42","modelId":"default-model","modelName":"Auto","isHelperMessage":false,"traceId":"2bcadbc8758317da706f385ce9eb37d8","toolStatus":{"call_669e6550df4f4d5aa96d74f1":{"ready":true,"status":"executed","args":{"filePath":"/Users/ff/Desktop/ProjectsAI/ProjectsHackathons/pawtner-emergency/PRD.md"},"result":{"status":"success","success":true,"result":{"type":"read_file_result","path":"/Users/ff/Desktop/ProjectsAI/ProjectsHackathons/pawtner-emergency/PRD.md","content":"     1:# Pawtner: Product Requirements Document
     2:
     3:| | |
     4:|---|---|
     5:| **Product** | Pawtner, an agentic medication-adherence companion for seniors |
     6:| **Event** | Tencent Cloud AI CAN DO IT Hackathon Singapore 2026, healthcare track |
     7:| **Deadline** | Friday 16 October 2026, 23:59 (GMT+8) |
     8:| **Status** | Draft v1, 13 October 2026 |
     9:| **Owners** | Person 1 (back end, "the brain"), Person 2 (front end, "the body"), Design track |
    10:| **Related docs** | `docs/BRIEF.md` (product brief), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/KANBAN.md`, `docs/DOG_BIBLE.md` |
    11:
    12:---
    13:
    14:## 1. Summary
    15:
    16:Pawtner is a phone app in which a senior looks after a virtual dog, and the dog's wellbeing depends on the senior's medication routine. The usual direction of care is reversed: **the dog depends on her**. A family caretaker manages the routine from a web dashboard and is only alerted when misses repeat.
    17:
    18:Behind the dog is an agent that checks the routine, decides when to nudge, refuses unsafe requests, and knows when to say "please ask a professional". Every decision it makes is visible, with the reason.
    19:
    20:## 2. Problem
    21:
    22:- Older adults on long-term medicines often miss or double doses, and find medicine labels and leaflets hard to understand.
    23:- Reminder apps feel clinical and nagging, and are easy to ignore.
    24:- Family caretakers want reassurance without turning care into surveillance.
    25:
    26:## 3. Users
    27:
    28:| User | Device | Needs | Design implications |
    29:|---|---|---|---|
    30:| **Senior** (primary) | Phone only | Remember doses, understand medicines, feel encouraged, never scolded | Big type, touch targets of at least 48 px, minimal words, read-aloud, warm tone |
    31:| **Caretaker** (secondary) | Web | Know things are OK, edit the routine, be told only when it matters | Weekly summaries, escalation settings, no medicine details in alerts |
    32:
    33:Names are always data, never code: the senior may be "Mum" or "Dad", the dog and caretaker can have any name. The demo uses fictional people: senior "Siew Lan" ("Mum"), caretaker "Jamie", dog "Max".
    34:
    35:## 4. Goals and non-goals
    36:
    37:### Goals (for this hackathon)
    38:1. A working **core loop** on a deployed URL: medicine → schedule → nudge → taken → dog reacts.
    39:2. **Visible agency**: judges can see what the agent noticed, what it decided, and why.
    40:3. **Responsible healthcare behaviour**: fixed safety rules, clear refusals, escalation to professionals.
    41:4. **Local relevance**: Singapore medicine registration data, local links, local places.
    42:
    43:### Non-goals
    44:- Clinical diagnosis or dosing advice of any kind.
    45:- Hardware, wearables or device integrations.
    46:- Real accounts, authentication or production-grade security (demo uses fictional data only).
    47:- HealthHub / Healthy365 integration, insurer or HPB partnerships (roadmap only).
    48:
    49:## 5. Success criteria
    50:
    51:| Criterion | Measure |
    52:|---|---|
    53:| Core loop works end to end | All three demo beats (section 13) run on the deployed URL without manual fixes |
    54:| Agent is visible | Every dog reaction has a decision log entry: rule, observations, reasoning, wording source |
    55:| Safety holds | All 4 shared fixtures pass; every refusal case in section 7.4 returns the expected refusal |
    56:| Failure is safe | With the model switched off, every decision still works using template messages |
    57:| Proof of tool usage | At least 3 chat screenshots required by the rules; target 10+ across CodeBuddy and Miora |
    58:
    59:---
    60:
    61:## 6. Core loop
    62:
    63:```
    64:Snap or enter a medicine
    65:  → check it is a registered product (HSA) and confirm the details
    66:  → plain-language explanation, read aloud
    67:  → set the schedule
    68:  → dog nudges at dose time
    69:  → senior taps "Taken" or snaps a photo
    70:  → dog stays happy, streak grows
    71:  → caretaker sees caring moments and a weekly summary
    72:```
    73:
    74:---
    75:
    76:## 7. The agent
    77:
    78:### 7.1 Design principle
    79:**Rules decide; the model only words things.** Every safety and escalation decision is made by deterministic rules with fixed thresholds. A language model is used only to write the dog's wording, write weekly summary prose, read a medicine label into fields the user must confirm, and rephrase trusted medicine text. If the model fails, times out or runs out of quota, the rule's decision stands and a pre-written template is used. The emergency path never calls the model.
    80:
    81:### 7.2 What the agent checks
    82:
    83:| Signal | Source |
    84:|---|---|
    85:| Dose status: upcoming, due, taken, skipped, missed | Derived from `med_schedules` + `dose_events` (missed is never stored) |
    86:| Consecutive missed doses | Derived from the ledger |
    87:| Blood pressure readings and free-text notes | `health_metrics` |
    88:| Days of supply left | `medications` |
    89:| Nudges already sent per dose | `agent_decisions` |
    90:| Caretaker consent and threshold | `user_caregivers` |
    91:
    92:### 7.3 What the agent decides on its own
    93:
    94:| Decision | Trigger (demo thresholds, configurable) | Dog mood |
    95:|---|---|---|
    96:| `nudge` (1st) | Dose not taken 60 min after scheduled time | sleepy |
    97:| `nudge` (2nd, last) | Still not taken 60 min after the 1st nudge | sleepy |
    98:| `nudge` + caretaker check-in | Consecutive missed doses ≥ caretaker threshold (minimum 2) **and** senior opted in | sleepy |
    99:| `celebrate` | Dose taken, walk finished, streak milestone | joyful |
   100:| `restock_reminder` | Days of supply ≤ 5 | content |
   101:| `doctor_question` | A note mentions a possible side effect (e.g. "sleepy", "dizzy", "nausea") → added to weekly summary as a question | content |
   102:| `see_gp_soon` | Reading ≥ 180 systolic or ≥ 120 diastolic **without** symptoms; or 3+ readings ≥ 140/90 in 7 days | attentive |
   103:| `emergency_995` | Reading ≥ 180 systolic or ≥ 120 diastolic **with** a symptom; or any note mentioning chest pain, breathlessness, fainting, confusion, one-sided weakness or slurred speech | attentive |
   104:| `stay_quiet` | Nothing needs attention | from heart score |
   105:
   106:**All thresholds are demo values, not clinical advice.** They live in one config file, never inside components.
   107:
   108:### 7.4 What the agent refuses
   109:
   110:| Request | Response |
   111:|---|---|
   112:| "I missed a dose, should I take two?" | Refuses. "Please don't take two. Check your label or ask your pharmacist what to do." |
   113:| Change, skip or stop a medicine | Refuses. Refers to doctor or pharmacist. |
   114:| "Is my reading fine?" | Never reassures. States the reading and what the rules recommend. |
   115:| Diagnosing a symptom | Refuses. Adds a doctor question, or escalates per 7.3. |
   116:| Identifying a pill from a photo | Refuses. A photo is logged as proof, never as verification. |
   117:| Medicine interactions | Refuses. Refers to pharmacist. |
   118:
   119:Every refusal is recorded in `agent_decisions.refused`.

   121:### 7.5 Escalation ladder
   122:
   123:1. Gentle in-app nudge (max 2 per dose)
   124:2. Doctor question added to weekly summary
   125:3. "Please see your GP soon" (calm, no playful animation)
   126:4. "Call 995 now" (calm, plain, no playful animation, no model call)
   127:5. Caretaker check-in, **only** on repeated misses and **only** with the senior's consent; never contains a medicine name
   128:
   129:### 7.6 Dog moods
   130:
   131:| Mood | When | Effects |
   132:|---|---|---|
   133:| joyful | heart 4, or right after `celebrate` | Bounce, sparkles |
   134:| content | heart 2–3, nothing due | Gentle breathing sway |

   136:| attentive | `see_gp_soon` or `emergency_995` | Still, upright, no playful effects |
   137:
   138:The dog is **never** sad, angry or crying. Mood is decided in one shared function, `selectDogMood(heart, latestDecision)`, and stored with each decision.
   139:
   140:### 7.7 Scores (demo formula, configurable)
   141:- **Heart (0–4):** share of today's due doses taken, scaled to 4 and rounded down; +1 if blood pressure was logged today; capped at 4. Starts at 2 when nothing is due yet.
   142:- **Streak:** consecutive days on which every scheduled dose was taken.
   143:- Both are cached on `dogs` and recomputed on every relevant write. No nightly job.

   153:| Local professional reference | Singapore National Drug Formulary (ndf.gov.sg) | **Link only** ("Check on NDF") | Reuse needs written MOH permission |
   154:| Local patient leaflets | HealthHub Medications A–Z | **Link only** ("Read the HealthHub leaflet") | Link only |

   157:If no trusted text exists: "Please ask your pharmacist", with no model call.

    11:
    12:---
    13:
    14:## 1. Summary
    15:
    16:Pawtner is a phone app in which a senior looks after a virtual dog, and the dog's wellbeing depends on the senior's medication routine. The usual direction of care is reversed: **the dog depends on her**. A family caretaker manages the routine from a web dashboard and is only alerted when misses repeat.
    17:
    18:Behind the dog is an agent that checks the routine, decides when to nudge, refuses unsafe requests, and knows when to say "please ask a professional". Every decision it makes is visible, with the reason.
    19:
    20:## 2. Problem
    21:
    22:- Older adults on long-term medicines often miss or double doses, and find medicine labels and leaflets hard to understand.
    23:- Reminder apps feel clinical and nagging, and are easy to ignore.
    24:- Family caretakers want reassurance without turning care into surveillance.
    25:
    26:## 3. Users
    27:
    28:| User | Device | Needs | Design implications |
    29:|---|---|---|---|
    30:| **Senior** (primary) | Phone only | Remember doses, understand medicines, feel encouraged, never scolded | Big type, touch targets of at least 48 px, minimal words, read-aloud, warm tone |
    31:| **Caretaker** (secondary) | Web | Know things are OK, edit the routine, be told only when it matters | Weekly summaries, escalation settings, no medicine details in alerts |
    32:
    33:Names are always data, never code: the senior may be "Mum" or "Dad", the dog and caretaker can have any name. The demo uses fictional people: senior "Siew Lan" ("Mum"), caretaker "Jamie", dog "Max".
    34:
    35:## 4. Goals and non-goals
    36:
    37:### Goals (for this hackathon)
    38:1. A working **core loop** on a deployed URL: medicine → schedule → nudge → taken → dog reacts.
    39:2. **Visible agency**: judges can see what the agent noticed, what it decided, and why.
    40:3. **Responsible healthcare behaviour**: fixed safety rules, clear refusals, escalation to professionals.
    41:4. **Local relevance**: Singapore medicine registration data, local links, local places.
    42:
    43:### Non-goals
    44:- Clinical diagnosis or dosing advice of any kind.
    45:- Hardware, wearables or device integrations.
    46:- Real accounts, authentication or production-grade security (demo uses fictional data only).
    47:- HealthHub / Healthy365 integration, insurer or HPB partnerships (roadmap only).
    48:
    49:## 5. Success criteria
    50:
    51:| Criterion | Measure |
    52:|---|---|
    53:| Core loop works end to end | All three demo beats (section 13) run on the deployed URL without manual fixes |
    54:| Agent is visible | Every dog reaction has a decision log entry: rule, observations, reasoning, wording source |
    55:| Safety holds | All 4 shared fixtures pass; every refusal case in section 7.4 returns the expected refusal |
    56:| Failure is safe | With the model switched off, every decision still works using template messages |
    57:| Proof of tool usage | At least 3 chat screenshots required by the rules; target 10+ across CodeBuddy and Miora |
    58:

    60:
    61:## 6. Core loop
    62:
    63:```
    64:Snap or enter a medicine
    65:  → check it is a registered product (HSA) and confirm the details
    66:  → plain-language explanation, read aloud
    67:  → set the schedule
    68:  → dog nudges at dose time
    69:  → senior taps "Taken" or snaps a photo
    70:  → dog stays happy, streak grows
    71:  → caretaker sees caring moments and a weekly summary
    72:```
    73:
    74:---
    75:
    76:## 7. The agent
    77:
    78:### 7.1 Design principle
    79:**Rules decide; the model only words things.** Every safety and escalation decision is made by deterministic rules with fixed thresholds. A language model is used only to write the dog's wording, write weekly summary prose, read a medicine label into fields the user must confirm, and rephrase trusted medicine text. If the model fails, times out or runs out of quota, the rule's decision stands and a pre-written template is used. The emergency path never calls the model.
    80:
    81:### 7.2 What the agent checks
    82:
    83:| Signal | Source |
    84:|---|---|
    85:| Dose status: upcoming, due, taken, skipped, missed | Derived from `med_schedules` + `dose_events` (missed is never stored) |
    86:| Consecutive missed doses | Derived from the ledger |
    87:| Blood pressure readings and free-text notes | `health_metrics` |
    88:| Days of supply left | `medications` |
    89:| Nudges already sent per dose | `agent_decisions` |
    90:| Caretaker consent and threshold | `user_caregivers` |
    91:
    92:### 7.3 What the agent decides on its own
    93:
    94:| Decision | Trigger (demo thresholds, configurable) | Dog mood |
    95:|---|---|---|
    96:| `nudge` (1st) | Dose not taken 60 min after scheduled time | sleepy |
    97:| `nudge` (2nd, last) | Still not taken 60 min after the 1st nudge | sleepy |
    98:| `nudge` + caretaker check-in | Consecutive missed doses ≥ caretaker threshold (minimum 2) **and** senior opted in | sleepy |
    99:| `celebrate` | Dose taken, walk finished, streak milestone | joyful |
   100:| `restock_reminder` | Days of supply ≤ 5 | content |
   101:| `doctor_question` | A note mentions a possible side effect (e.g. "sleepy", "dizzy", "nausea") → added to weekly summary as a question | content |
   102:| `see_gp_soon` | Reading ≥ 180 systolic or ≥ 120 diastolic **without** symptoms; or 3+ readings ≥ 140/90 in 7 days | attentive |
   103:| `emergency_995` | Reading ≥ 180 systolic or ≥ 120 diastolic **with** a symptom; or any note mentioning chest pain, breathlessness, fainting, confusion, one-sided weakness or slurred speech | attentive |
   104:| `stay_quiet` | Nothing needs attention | from heart score |
   105:
   106:**All thresholds are demo values, not clinical advice.** They live in one config file, never inside components.
   107:

   110:| Request | Response |
   111:|---|---|
   112:| "I missed a dose, should I take two?" | Refuses. "Please don't take two. Check your label or ask your pharmacist what to do." |
   113:| Change, skip or stop a medicine | Refuses. Refers to doctor or pharmacist. |
   114:| "Is my reading fine?" | Never reassures. States the reading and what the rules recommend. |
   115:| Diagnosing a symptom | Refuses. Adds a doctor question, or escalates per 7.3. |
   116:| Identifying a pill from a photo | Refuses. A photo is logged as proof, never as verification. |
   117:| Medicine interactions | Refuses. Refers to pharmacist. |

   119:Every refusal is recorded in `agent_decisions.refused`.

   129:### 7.6 Dog moods

   132:|---|---|---|
   133:| joyful | heart 4, or right after `celebrate` | Bounce, sparkles |
   134:| content | heart 2–3, nothing due | Gentle breathing sway |
   135:| sleepy | heart 0–1, or a `nudge` | Slow droop, "zzz". Waiting, never sad |
   136:| attentive | `see_gp_soon` or `emergency_995` | Still, upright, no playful effects |
   137:
   138:The dog is **never** sad, angry or crying. Mood is decided in one shared function, `selectDogMood(heart, latestDecision)`, and stored with each decision.

   142:- **Streak:** consecutive days on which every scheduled dose was taken.
   143:- Both are cached on `dogs` and recomputed on every relevant write. No nightly job.

   188:| T1-18 | Dog assets: base dog + 4-mood sheet + garden background | Design | Same dog in all moods; dog clearly visible in a greyscale check |

   190:### 9.2 Tier 2: Should have
   191:
   192:| ID | Requirement | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
   193:|---|---|---|---|
   194:| T2-01 | HSA register import + product search API | P1 | Search by brand or ingredient returns registered products; source credited |
   195:| T2-02 | Label photo reading → fields + HSA match → **user confirms** | P1 + P2 | Nothing is saved before confirmation; manual entry always available |
   196:| T2-03 | Medicine explanation from MedlinePlus, with rephrase + code check | P1 | Rephrase containing a new number or name is rejected and the source text is shown |
   197:| T2-04 | Explanation screen with read-aloud, credits, NDF and HealthHub links | P2 | Read-aloud works; links open in a new tab |
   198:| T2-05 | "What did your doctor say it's for?" field | P2 | Shown first when filled; never filled by the model |
   199:| T2-06 | Medication + schedule editing on `/care` | P1 + P2 | Changes appear on the phone after refresh |
   200:| T2-07 | Photo proof and label photo upload to object storage | P1 + P2 | DB stores URLs only |
   201:| T2-08 | Real GPS walk (foreground only): distance, noise filter, speed check, wake lock | P2 | Points with accuracy worse than ~30 m ignored; >12 km/h for 30 s pauses distance; **no route stored** |
   202:| T2-09 | Souvenirs from cumulative distance (Singapore landmarks) | P1 + P2 | Thresholds in `shared/souvenirs.ts`, not in components |

   222:---
   223:
   224:## 10. Experience requirements
   225:
   226:### Phone (senior)
   227:- Storybook look: crocheted garden background, one crocheted dog, sun or moon.
   228:- Layers, back to front: background → sun/moon → soft glow → dog (separate image) with shadow → UI.
   229:- Top: dog name + 4-heart meter (left), settings (right). Below the dog: "Today" (left), streak + treat (right).
   230:- Large white rounded card (24 px radius) over the bottom half: today's schedule. Each row: time, medicine + strength, Taken / photo action. Friendly empty state.
   231:- Floating white pill tab bar (Home, Milestones, Health) and a round black paw "+" button.
   232:- Nunito; touch targets of at least 48 px; read-aloud on explanations.
   233:- Tone: warm and playful, never clinical, never nagging. Serious messages are calm and plain.
   234:
   235:### Web (caretaker)
   236:- Phone app on desktop: centred 430 px column, never stretched.
   237:- `/care` uses the full width: weekly summary, medication editing (photo upload instead of camera), nudge and escalation settings, caretaker list.
   238:- "The phone is where care happens; the web is where care is managed."
   239:
   240:---
   241:
   242:## 11. Privacy and safety
   243:
   244:- Caretakers see caring moments only; alerts never contain medicine names.
   245:- Escalation requires the senior's explicit opt-in; minimum threshold of 2 consecutive misses is enforced in the database.
   246:- Walks store distance and time only, never the route.
   247:- Photos stored in object storage; the database keeps URLs only.
   248:- The model never makes safety decisions, never fills `prescribed_for`, and can only rephrase trusted text.
   249:- Demo uses fictional data only; this is stated in the submission.
   250:
   251:---
   252:
   253:## 12. Technical summary
   254:
   255:| Layer | Choice |
   256:|---|---|
   257:| App | Vite + React + TypeScript PWA, mobile-first; routes `/` (senior) and `/care` (caretaker) |
   258:| API | Stateless serverless functions in a Node runtime |
   259:| Database | PostgreSQL, provider-neutral, plain SQL migrations, `pg` driver |
   260:| Photos | S3-compatible object storage (Tier 2) |
   261:| Model | Tencent Cloud TokenHub, OpenAI-compatible, free trial quota, post-paid billing disabled |
   262:| Config | Environment variables only: `DATABASE_URL`, `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, `VITE_API_BASE_URL` |
   263:| Data model | users, caregivers, user_caregivers, dogs, medications, med_schedules, dose_events (ledger), health_metrics, walk_sessions, souvenirs, agent_decisions, sg_registered_products |
   264:
   265:Full detail in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
   266:
   267:---
   268:
   269:## 13. Demo script (about 90 seconds)
   270:
   271:| Beat | What happens | What judges see |
   272:|---|---|---|
   273:| 1. Missed dose | Demo clock passes 10:00; morning dose not taken | Dog turns sleepy; gentle nudge; decision log shows rule + reasoning. Second miss → caretaker check-in on `/care`, no medicine name |
   274:| 2. Emergency | Senior logs 185/120 + "bad headache" | Dog turns attentive; calm "Call 995 now"; no model used; decision log shows the rule |
   275:| 3. Weekly summary + walk | Sunday summary; simulated walk | Doctor question drafted from "feel sleepy at night"; dog dizzy on the bus stretch, souvenir unlocked, joyful dog |
   276:
   277:---
   278:
   279:## 14. Timeline
   280:
   281:| When | Person 1 | Person 2 | Design / together |
   282:|---|---|---|---|
   283:| Tue 13 Oct | Choose Postgres provider + hosting runtime; claim TokenHub trial | Push repo; run CodeBuddy Prompt 1 | Dog bible; Miora base dog + garden |

   286:| Fri 16 Oct | Tier 2 until 15:00; write-up | Tier 2 until 15:00; demo video | Cover image; screenshots sorted; **submit by 20:00** |

   288:---
   289:
   290:## 15. Risks
   291:
   292:| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
   293:|---|---|---|
   294:| Hosting runtime can't connect to Postgres | Medium | Decide hosting before writing API code; fallback to any Node serverless host |
   295:| Model quota or outage during demo | Medium | Template fallback for every decision |
   296:| Dog images inconsistent across moods | Medium | Expression sheet in one generation; CSS motion/overlay fallback on a single image |
   297:| GPS unreliable indoors | High | "Simulate walk" is the demo path |
   298:| Two people editing the contract at once | Medium | Announce before editing; log in `DECISIONS.md` |
   299:| Scope creep | High | Tier 2 only after Tier 1 passes on the deployed URL |
   300:| Missing proof screenshots | Low if handled | Each person screenshots their own tool chats into `proof/` as they work |
